papers.title: An approximate control variates approach to multifidelity distribution estimation
papers.abstract: Forward simulation-based uncertainty quantification that studies the distribution of quantities of interest (QoI) is a crucial component for computationally robust engineering design and prediction. There is a large body of literature devoted to accurately assessing statistics of QoIs, and in particular, multilevel or multifidelity approaches are known to be effective, leveraging cost-accuracy tradeoffs between a given ensemble of models. However, effective algorithms that can estimate the full distribution of QoIs are still under active development. In this paper, we introduce a general multifidelity framework for estimating the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of a vector-valued QoI associated with a high-fidelity model under a budget constraint. Given a family of appropriate control variates obtained from lower-fidelity surrogates, our framework involves identifying the most cost-effective model subset and then using it to build an approximate control variates estimator for the target CDF. We instantiate the framework by constructing a family of control variates using intermediate linear approximators and rigorously analyze the corresponding algorithm. Our analysis reveals that the resulting CDF estimator is uniformly consistent and asymptotically optimal as the budget tends to infinity, with only mild moment and regularity assumptions on the joint distribution of QoIs. The approach provides a robust multifidelity CDF estimator that is adaptive to the available budget, does not require \textit{a priori} knowledge of cross-model statistics or model hierarchy, and applies to multiple dimensions. We demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the approach using test examples of parametric PDEs and stochastic differential equations including both academic instances and more challenging engineering problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种基于近似控制变量的多保真度分布估计方法，可高效解决仿真采样效率问题，适用于不确定性量化，但未涉及植入物力学或生物力学设计的具体应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address implant or biomechanics design, lacks experimental validation in a biomedical context, and focuses on general PDEs and SDEs rather than constrained optimization or point predictions.

summary_zh.motivation: 高效估计复杂仿真模型的输出分布，以支持鲁棒设计。
summary_zh.method: 利用低保真度模型构建近似控制变量，自适应选择模型子集估计累计分布函数。
summary_zh.result: 所提估计器一致且渐近最优，适用于多维输出。
summary_zh.validation: 通过参数化PDE和随机微分方程数值算例验证。

summary_en.motivation: Efficient estimation of the full distribution of quantities of interest from expensive simulations is critical for robust design.
summary_en.method: A general multifidelity framework using approximate control variates from lower-fidelity surrogates selects cost-effective model subsets to estimate the cumulative distribution function.
summary_en.result: The resulting estimator is uniformly consistent and asymptotically optimal as the budget grows, with mild assumptions.
summary_en.validation: The approach is validated on parametric PDEs and stochastic differential equations, including both academic and engineering examples.

papers.title: ReBound: An Open-Source 3D Bounding Box Annotation Tool for Active Learning
papers.abstract: In recent years, supervised learning has become the dominant paradigm for training deep-learning based methods for 3D object detection. Lately, the academic community has studied 3D object detection in the context of autonomous vehicles (AVs) using publicly available datasets such as nuScenes and Argoverse 2.0. However, these datasets may have incomplete annotations, often only labeling a small subset of objects in a scene. Although commercial services exists for 3D bounding box annotation, these are often prohibitively expensive. To address these limitations, we propose ReBound, an open-source 3D visualization and dataset re-annotation tool that works across different datasets. In this paper, we detail the design of our tool and present survey results that highlight the usability of our software. Further, we show that ReBound is effective for exploratory data analysis and can facilitate active-learning. Our code and documentation is available at https://github.com/ajedgley/ReBound

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是关于自动驾驶中3D目标检测的标注工具，与有限元代理建模完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA, surrogate modelling, uncertainty quantification, constraints handling, or biomechanics/implant design; it is a pure computer vision annotation tool for autonomous driving.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有3D检测数据集标注不完整且商业工具昂贵，需要开源标注工具
summary_zh.method: 开发了跨数据集的3D可视化与重标注工具ReBound，支持主动学习
summary_zh.result: 工具可用性调查显示良好，能有效进行探索性数据分析和主动学习
summary_zh.validation: 通过用户调查和演示案例验证工具实用性

summary_en.motivation: Existing 3D object detection datasets suffer from incomplete annotations and costly commercial tools, motivating an open-source annotation solution.
summary_en.method: We propose ReBound, an open-source 3D visualization and re-annotation tool that works across multiple autonomous driving datasets and supports active learning.
summary_en.result: User surveys and case studies demonstrate the tool's usability and effectiveness for exploratory data analysis and active learning.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through user surveys and illustrative use cases without quantitative benchmarking.

papers.title: Tailoring the theory of critical distances to better assess the combined effect of complex geometries and process-inherent defects during the fatigue assessment of SLM Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: This work aims to apply the Theory of Critical Distances (TCD) to the fatigue assessment of additively manufactured (AM) Ti-6Al-4V material produced via the selective laser melting (SLM) process. Modified alternatives to traditional TCD methods are considered. In this sense, it is sought to develop a fatigue prediction model that is better suited to assessing the impact of multiple stress-rising features which are located in close proximity to each other. Hereby, consideration has been given to modelling process-inherent surface roughness in combination with an internally positioned artificial defect, shaped as a feature that is reminiscent of a pore. Simultaneously, the research also seeks to circumnavigate a potential issue with respect to the current TCD methodology. This concerns the matter of applying TCD practices to components whereby the area of interest for conducting stress-distance analytics is on a size scale that is smaller than that of the critical distance length parameter itself. Several different strategies were attempted as a way to try and achieve meaningful modifications to the TCD process. Results show that it is possible to overcome such challenges that can often present themselves during the fatigue appraisal of AM metal parts. In this sense, the optimal novel strategy that was experimented with returned average error margins of 13.7% or better. It is anticipated that such models may assist in further optimising the accuracy of service life evaluation for metallic AM components that are intended for industry.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM Ti-6Al-4V的疲劳评估方法，对理解增材制造植入物的疲劳性能有参考价值，但未涉及应力遮挡或骨整合等核心问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures, stress shielding, stiffness matching, or osseointegration; it focuses only on fatigue prediction methodology for SLM Ti-6Al-4V with defects.

summary_zh.motivation: 改进临界距离理论，用于评估SLM Ti-6Al-4V中复杂几何和缺陷的联合疲劳效应。
summary_zh.method: 提出修正的TCD方法，处理小尺度下多个应力集中特征的相互作用。
summary_zh.result: 最优新策略的平均误差在13.7%以内，提高了疲劳寿命预测精度。
summary_zh.validation: 通过含缺陷SLM Ti-6Al-4V试样的疲劳实验数据验证模型。

summary_en.motivation: To adapt the Theory of Critical Distances for fatigue assessment of SLM Ti-6Al-4V by addressing multiple stress-rising features at small scales.
summary_en.method: Modified TCD strategies were developed to model combined effects of surface roughness and internal defects below the critical distance length.
summary_en.result: The optimal novel strategy achieved average prediction errors of 13.7% or better.
summary_en.validation: The model was validated against fatigue experiments on SLM Ti-6Al-4V specimens with engineered defects and surface roughness.
